subject: June 16 service gap: concise timeline, mitigations, verification request
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: June 16 service gap: concise timeline, mitigations, verification request

Hi Emily —

Thank you again for your patience while we completed our internal investigation into the June 16 service gap that impacted NovusPay tokenization calls between 14:10–14:46 UTC. Attached is a concise RCA summary (redwood_rca_summary_20260618.pdf), a bundle of sanitized logs we used in the analysis (logs_novuspay_20260616.tar.gz), and the rollout plan for the patch we intend to ship (patch_rollout_plan.md).

High level (TL;DR):
- Root cause: an autoscaler race combined with an unexpected KV-cache eviction during a traffic spike, which led to transient stale cache references and increased token processing latency.
- Impact window: 2026-06-16T14:10:23Z — 2026-06-16T14:46:07Z (partial request failures, elevated latencies for ~36 minutes).
- Customer-visible: intermittent 5xx errors for ~18% of requests during the peak and per-token latency degradation for the remainder.
- Immediate mitigation completed: configuration rollback and temporary guards to prevent concurrent autoscaler operations (completed same day).
- Next actions: engineered fix (race lock + improved eviction policy), staged rollout, and verification checklist for NovusPay to run after rollout.

Request: please review the attached RCA and logs and confirm whether you want Redwood to run the verification window on your behalf (we can coordinate a 30-minute test tomorrow) or if NovusPay prefers to run the short checklist we include below.

We recognize the severity and are proposing the following commitments:
- Marissa (engineering lead) will own the patch, with a target staged rollout on 2026-06-20 (can accelerate if you prefer).
- Rishi (reliability) will run post-rollout verification and share telemetry excerpts within 24 hours of completion.
- Redwood will provide a one-off service credit if the impact exceeded your SLA thresholds; we’ll follow up with accounting after we align on the verified impact window.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the timeline and the verification steps if that helps.

Apologies again — we know this disrupted your flow.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_rca_summary_20260618.pdf, logs_novuspay_20260616.tar.gz, patch_rollout_plan.md

Subject: Re: June 16 service gap: concise timeline, mitigations, verification request

Thanks, Dylan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions up front:
1) Can you confirm whether any sensitive token material was exposed or persisted by the cache miss behavior? Ops and Legal are particularly concerned about persistence and retention.
2) How are you planning to validate the fix? We need a concrete verification plan so we can clear this internally.
3) Please outline the SLA credit path and required confirmation steps — we’ll need that for our procurement team.

We can do a call tomorrow morning (PST) if that helps.

—Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Infrastructure, NovusPay
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: June 16 service gap: concise timeline, mitigations, verification request

Emily — thanks for the questions. Quick answers below and more detail in the attached RCA. Quoting your questions for clarity.

> 1) Can you confirm whether any sensitive token material was exposed or persisted by the cache miss behavior?

Short answer: No. The KV cache held ephemeral references to in-memory tokenized payloads; there was no disk persistence of token material, and our review of retention logs shows no off-host export. We have a dedicated log slice in logs_novuspay_20260616.tar.gz that shows no write-to-disk activity for token buffers during the window (see rca section 2.1). We will also run an additional targeted retention scan and share results by end of day today.

> 2) How are you planning to validate the fix?

Planned validation (summary):
- Unit + regression tests pushed to CI (completed).
- Canary rollout in one AZ for 4 hours under mirrored traffic for verification (Marissa owns).
- Synthetic verification: a 30-minute scripted workload that reproduces the prior spike pattern while measuring error rates and per-token latency. Expected outcome: 99.9% success within normal latency band.
- Post-canary: 24-hour telemetry review and a quick artifacts package we’ll send you (metrics + sanitized logs).

If you prefer Redwood to run the synthetic check against your tenant, we can do that in a scheduled window and share the results live.

> 3) SLA credit path and confirmation steps

We’ll work with our billing team once the verified impact window is finalized. Proposed flow: you confirm the impacted request set after we share the post-rollout telemetry -> Redwood issues an itemized credit proposal -> you approve -> we apply the credit. I’ll loop Finance once we align.

Action owners & target dates:
- Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com): patch PR + canary rollout plan — target 2026-06-20.
- Rishi Malhotra (rishi.malhotra@redwood.com): verification run & telemetry extract — target within 24h of canary success.
- Dylan Brooks (me): coordinate verification call and billing handoff.

If that timeline works I’ll schedule the canary and verification window and send calendar invites.

Thanks — Dylan

Internal notes / plan (internal recipients only):

1) Patch summary: introduce a per-pool autoscaler lock + conservative cache-eviction watermark. Patch PR is at: https://redwood.internal/pulls/4523 (private). I’ve attached the rollout checklist to patch_rollout_plan.md.

2) Canary plan:
- Canary AZ: us-west-2a.
- Mirror traffic: 10% of peak (non-customer affecting).
- Canary window: 2026-06-20 14:00–18:00 UTC.
- Rollback threshold: >0.5% increase in 5xx or >20% change in per-token latency percentile P99.

3) Verification artifacts to share to customer:
- Canary telemetry (timeseries + aggregated error counts).
- Sanitized logs slice (same as attached).
- Short writeup of what changed in the eviction path.

4) Owner reminders:
- Marissa: push PR + schedule canary calendar invite (target 2026-06-19 internal review).
- Rishi: prepare the telemetry extraction notebook and mean/percentile tables for the customer report.

I’ll coordinate with Dylan to send the confirmed canary window to NovusPay once Dylan confirms. Also adding the Google Drive folder for verification artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExample

-Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novuspay.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Verification steps and short checklist

Hi Emily — following up with the short verification steps we mentioned. These are lightweight and safe to run; if you prefer Redwood to run them we can do that in the agreed window.

Verification checklist (expected duration: 30 min):
1) Warmed token calls: send 500 representative tokenization requests over 10 minutes (steady arrival). Expectation: <0.5% 5xx, P95 latency within historical baseline.
2) Spike replay: replay the provided synthetic burst (we include the replay script in the Drive folder). Expectation: no transient 5xx tail beyond historical baseline; per-token latency P99 should not exceed prior observed maxima.
3) Sanity log check: confirm no write-to-disk activity for token buffers in the local log sample (we’ll share grep commands to run).

If the checks pass we’ll mark the canary as successful and produce the telemetry package for your review. If you’d like a Redwood engineer to be on the call while you run step 1–2, we’re happy to be available.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
